note: The layouts this package reads and writes, pinned to the figures Nintendo printed. An exhaustive walk of a format proves the package round-trips itself; it cannot prove the format is the one the hardware uses. These figures are what makes the difference, and every one was read off a rendered page rather than out of the scan's text layer.

order: hardware.json, for anything Nintendo printed: which byte holds which plane, which bits hold a character code, how a colour is packed
an exhaustive walk of the format, for anything that follows from those figures by enumeration rather than by judgement
an independent reading of the same figures, pinned in pinned.json, for whether the figures were read correctly here at all

ares's source at the commit each entry in divergences.json names, for the Mode 7 offset width, the bits each Mode 7 product keeps and the two unprinted object size settings, none of which the manual prints
real cartridge bytes, for whether the published grouping is the one that holds pictures
authority.why:
These are layouts rather than silicon, and the input spaces are small enough to walk from end to end, so the second rung is enumeration rather than a recording. Every two-bit tile that can exist is decoded and re-encoded, which leaves no case untried.

What that cannot do is catch a misreading. Every figure here was read off a rendered page by one person and written into this file; the code is held to this file, and the walk proves the code agrees with itself. Swap the two flip bits here and in the code together and all of it still passes, because a consistently wrong decoder round-trips perfectly. So the third rung is somebody else's reading of the same figures, and it sits below the figures because it cannot overrule them: it answers whether they were read right, not what they say.
authority.whatIsMissing: A console. The layout is no longer held only to a second reading of the manual: conformance/against_cartridges.py reads real cartridge bytes three ways and asks which reading finds the most structure, and the published one wins 52.5% of 11,765 regions against a floor of 33.3%. What is still absent is a rendered frame from hardware, which is the only thing that would settle what a pixel looks like rather than how the bytes are grouped.

comparedAgainst.what: An independent reading of the same figures, lifted from a pinned commit, and separately 11,765 regions of real cartridge data read three ways.
comparedAgainst.why: A second reading catches a misreading of the manual. It cannot catch two readers making the same mistake. Cartridge bytes can, because a picture read with the wrong grouping stops looking like a picture.

characterData.title: CHR DATA CONSTRUCTION
characterData.note: A character is eight rows of eight dots. Each row contributes one byte to each bit plane, and the planes are stored in pairs: the two bytes of a row's first pair sit in one sixteen bit word, and each further pair starts eight words later.

depths.quote: V-RAM address for a CHR data (8 word) is as follows: n+N(Name)x8~n+Nx8+7
V-RAM address for a CHR data (16 word) is as follows: n+N(Name)x16~n+Nx16+15
V-RAM address for a CHR data (32 word) is as follows: n+N(Name)x 32~n+Nx32+31

fields.name: COLOR
fields.meaningQuote: COLOR PALETTE <8-Palettes> SELECT: Palette designation per character

fields.name: BG Pri.
fields.meaningQuote: BG PRIORITY: Determine the display priority per character in case OBJ and BG1 ~ BG4 are combined on the same screen.

colour.channelOrderQuote: Blue Green Red, the field order of register 2132H, Color Brilliance Data

transparent.quote: The top color data of each CG color data palette is transparent. Because transparent is a color which is not displayed, any color can be set. The color data of CG address (00H) is normally black (background).

colour.channelBitsQuote: CG-RAM COLOR DATA. BLUE GREEN RED. D15 | d14 | d13 | d12 | d11 | d10 | d9 | d8 | d7 | d6 | d5 | d4 | d3 | d2 | d1 | d0
colour.howTheWidthWasSettled: By the figure rather than by arithmetic. The appendix prints the colour word as fifteen cells under three labels, five cells to each of BLUE, GREEN and RED, with D15 outside them. That page is a picture with nothing in the text layer, so it was rendered and read; the same figure prints DIRECT SELECT COLOR DATA beneath it, which is how the direct colour packing is laid out.

objectData.title: OBJECT DATA
objectData.note: Read off the rendered page. Each object takes two words at OAM addresses 2n and 2n+1, and words 256 to 271 hold two more bits for each of eight objects. The bits are drawn as D15 to D0 of a word, whose low byte is the first byte in memory.

highTable.positionMsbQuote: The base position of the OBJ on the H-direction will be determined by both H-position (8-bit) and the H-position MSB.
highTable.sizeQuote: Size Large/Small: Determine the size to be used either of 2 OBJ's by register <2101H>.

fields.name: OBJ PRIORITY
fields.meaningQuote: Determine the display priority when OBJ is combined with BG1 ~ BG4 (per character).

position.quote: The H-position is a complementary expression of 2 (9-bit).

objectSizes.title: OBJSEL
objectSizes.note: The table under register 2101H, read off the rendered page. Each row is one setting of S2 S1 S0 and gives the small and the large size in dots; every size printed is square. Settings 110 and 111 are not printed, and divergences.json records where those two come from.

matrix.quote: The most significant bit of the upper 8-bit is for the signed bit. (MP15 is the signed bit. There is a decimal point between M7 & M8.)

formula.note: Printed as a picture. X0 and Y0 are the centre, X1 and Y1 the display coordinate, X2 and Y2 the coordinate before calculation. Appendix page A-16 prints the same transform. Neither says how wide the difference is or how many bits each product keeps, and divergences.json records what ares does there.

centre.quote: The coordinate value of X0 & Y0 can be designated by 13-bit (complement of 2).

notStated: Anything about timing. These are layouts in memory; when the PPU reads them is a different question and not one this package asks.
What the hardware does with a character code above the range the field can hold, since the field cannot hold one.

How wide the scroll offset minus the centre is when the Mode 7 multiplier takes it, and how many bits each product keeps. The formula on page 2-27-9 says neither; divergences.json records what ares does.
Object size settings 110 and 111, which the table on page 2-27-1 does not print; divergences.json records what ares does.
